text:
Kevin: Nightly perf job showed a big regression in comm/compute overlap for a TP/PP run (tp=2 pp=2). All GPUs idle on compute stream while NCCL allreduce sits in a long wait state. Suspect interaction between CUDA graph capture and KV-cache prefetch.

infra-bot: CI run: https://ci.redwood/2205/8342 — failed perf threshold :warning:

Kevin: Quick repro (from the perf runner):
```
python -m tests.e2e_infer --model=redwood-opus-70b --tp=2 --pp=2 --batch-limit=32 --use-kv-prefetch --cuda-graph=auto
```
Logs: kernel selection switches to fallback reduction path after a certain token boundary, then allreduce latency spikes x8. Pasting trimmed trace below.

Kevin: TRACE: gpu0: capture(stream=2) start -> launch fp16_gemm -> host-sync -> capture end -> ncclAllReduce waiting on event(2)

Rachael: Can you paste the nvprof / nsight timeline? Is there a host-side stall (cudaLaunch) or is it stream ordering? :eyes:

Kevin: nvprof shows host activity at the same time as capture end (tiny memcpy for kv warmup). Timeline snippet:
```
Host  13:22:11.120 memcpy H2D kv_prefetch  2.1ms
GPU0 13:22:11.123 kernel fp16_ff  0.9ms (stream 3)
GPU0 13:22:11.124 cudaEventRecord(ev_capture, stream=2)
GPU0 13:22:11.124 ncclAllReduce(..., stream=1) WAIT on ev_capture -> stalls 6.5ms
```

Simon: I profiled a minimized run. Two things jumped out: 1) kernel-selection heuristic flips to an unoptimized reduction kernel when the micro-batch boundary increases (our batching heuristic picks bigger microbatches when `--batch-limit>=32`) which forces a different kernel path; 2) CUDA graph capture is capturing the prefetch stream event ordering which ends up serialized with NCCL because of event-record ordering across streams.

Simon: Essentially, capture serializes an event on the capture stream which we then `cudaEventSynchronize`/record-wait across the NCCL stream during replay -> no overlap. The runtime's capture-friendly path didn't insert `cudaStreamWaitEvent` properly with the desired record/wait semantics for priority streams.

Luis: Workarounds I tried locally: disable capture for kv-prefetch (`--no-cuda-graph-prefetch`) and the overlap returns. Also reducing `--batch-limit` to 28 keeps kernel-selection on optimized path and avoids the fallback.

Rachael: That fits with our batching heuristics. We recently changed threshold from 30->32 to reduce micro-batch variance; side effect is it triggers a different kernel selector in kernel_selector.cpp.

Simon: I ran a kernel-selection trace (attached gist): kernel_selector picks `reduce_generic_fp32` instead of `reduce_opt_fp16` once effective microbatch tokens > 512. The selector uses an estimated shared-memory pressure heuristic that wasn't accounting for kv-cache prefetch buffers.

Kevin: So two levers: keep kernel selector aware of kv-prefetch footprint OR avoid capture of the prefetch/control streams (or use separate non-captured stream for nccl). Which is safer for e2e? I'm leaning to a short-term guard: change capture to exclude kv-prefetch and add a batching clamp in the runtime to avoid the >512 tokens corner.

Simon: I'll prepare a small PR: (a) add `--no-cuda-graph-prefetch` runtime flag defaulting to off for now, (b) clamp batching heuristic to 30-48 window to avoid selector flip, (c) add an assert in kernel_selector that logs when prefetch allocs could change shared mem estimate. I'll also add a unit test reproducer using `--tp=1 --pp=2` so it's fast.

Kevin: Can you also try forcing stream priorities? Maybe capture should use low-priority stream so NCCL on high-priority can preempt. Patch suggestion: `cudaStreamCreateWithPriority(&s, cudaStreamNonBlocking, lowPriority)` for capture/kv streams.

Simon: Good idea. I tried priority tweak: it reduced stall but didn't eliminate it — because the capture-instantiated graph still records the event ordering that NCCL waits on. So priority helps but doesn't fix the captured synchronization semantics.

Luis: For triage: 1) Simon opens PR with the capture opt-out + batching clamp; 2) Rachael files kernel_selector bug to track shared-memory accounting; 3) Kevin schedules a nightly run with `--no-cuda-graph-prefetch` to verify perf baseline.

Rachael: Also add a perf test variant that exercises the kernel-selector boundary with kv-prefetch on to detect regressions in CI.

infra-bot: Job queued: perf/nightly/2205/kv-capture-guard — results ETA 02:00

Kevin: Thanks team. Simon, assign me on the PR for review. Let's keep the rollback path (capture off) simple so SRE can flip if needed. :thumbsup:

Simon: on it, will push a draft in the next 2 hours. :party:

Luis: If we want long-term fix, kernel_selector needs a model for allocator footprints (kv cache + prefetch) when estimating kernels. I'll take that for the follow-up.

Kevin: Great. If the nightly with capture disabled looks good we'll roll the guard into the 2.14.1 hotfix.
